title: Claude Code skill researches 20-40 web pages and turns any topic into a cited audio course
summary: Courses on sites like Udemy are fixed and long. This skill has Claude research a topic across 20-40 web pages, compare where sources agree and disagree, and produce about 12 two-minute two-voice audio lessons, each with a summary card and citations.
agent_role: The agent maps sub-topics, researches and reads sources with reader agents, merges themes, plans and writes lessons, and generates audio. The human reviews one sample lesson before the rest are made.
outcome: The author says a 12-lesson course takes one long Claude Code session and yields about 25 minutes of audio.
what_they_did: Assaf Kipnis built Claudemy, a Claude Code skill. You ask it to "teach me [topic]". It maps the topic into sub-topics and researches 20–40 web pages, with no more than 3 from any one site. Reader agents take cited notes, and the skill merges them into themes with counts of how many sources agree. It then plans about 12 two-minute lessons, makes one sample lesson, and waits for the user's reaction before writing and recording the rest. Audio uses ElevenLabs or the free macOS voices.
how_it_went: The author says a 12-lesson course takes one long Claude Code session and produces about 25 minutes of audio. Each lesson comes with a card, and the course comes with a playbook.
worth_knowing: A checker rejects any lesson that cites a page the research didn't actually read. Without an ElevenLabs key, the skill falls back to plainer macOS voices. Health, legal and financial topics get a note that the advice depends on your situation.
prompt: Teach me [topic] at a [beginner/intermediate] level. Research 20–40 web pages from practitioners, official docs, research summaries and a few dissenting views, with no more than 3 from any one site. Take cited notes, group them into themes, and show how many sources agree on each point and where they disagree. Plan about 12 two-minute lessons, foundations first. Write one sample lesson as a two-host script with a three-line summary, one thing to try and source links, then wait for my feedback before writing the rest. Only cite pages you actually read.

curation.rationale: The multi-step research-to-audio workflow is clear and reproducible, with source checks and agent roles spelled out. However, the README shows no specific course built or result achieved, so it is borderline; the score includes a small education boost.
